utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I was the chief of that administration, so it is very difficult for me to say; however, before the Trial Chamber, I have to say it. This administration was on a par -- or, rather, what the General Staff was for the Supreme Command, that's what this administration was for the General Staff. Or let me define this in different words. The 1st Administration was a staff administrative coordinating interbranch professional organ, which used to perform functional tasks. I've used --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That administration as well as all the other organs had its own -- its basic function. It had other functions and tasks. And it says here very clearly. But could you please use your own words and tell us what the basic function of the 1st Administration was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The basic functions of the 1st Administration were multi-fold. There were maybe eight or nine of them, but the most important was the planning, the engagement and combat readiness of the Army of Yugoslavia; planning the elements or devising the strategical elements of the development of VJ; the preparation of terrain; scientific and research work within the area of military skills.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like to ask you something else. What is the connection between the administration and the border?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: State border security was one of its tasks and functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move to the following page in B/C/S and can we also display page 2 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When we were talking about the principles or basic principles laid out at the beginning of this order, you told us what the sense of this order was. This is very clearly spelled out. But could you please tell us, when it come to the 1st Administration, who did the 1st Administration command?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The 1st Administration, and this applies to all of the organisational units, commands its own subordinated organisations and units. Let me be more specific. The 1st Administration had the first department, a second department, a department for operations and general planning. They are a section for state border and operational centre. Those were its organisational units that the 1st Administration was composed of and it was also immediately or directly linked to the military and geographic institute, but that was not an organisational unit of the General Staff but it -- it was outside of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down. I can see that you speak slowly fairly, but funnily enough the interpreter is having difficulty keeping pace with you. So if you could try to slow down as you speak, sir, I would appreciate it very much.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours. I get carried away in testifying. I will try to avoid being cautioned in the future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let me now ask you the following. The tasks are listed here. I will only ask you about some. The first task mentioned here monitors and assesses the military and security situation in the surrounding countries, and issues orders as to the taking of measures for the defence of the country. Is this basically the most important or maybe the upper-most task of the 1st Administration?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: I agree with you that this is one of the important tasks of the 1st Administration, because any surprise is meant to be prevented by that. Let me repeat: The monitoring and assessment of the military and political situation in the territory, the territorial waters and the air-space, a professional assessment of the situation, the drawing of conclusions as to how that situation affects the security of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and, in accordance with that, it proposes that certain measures be taken, measures of combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't see on the document what are you talking about. What you said in your question and the answer, I don't see on the document. You asked the question: "The first task mentioned here monitors and assesses the military and security situation in the surrounding countries, and issues orders as to the taking of measures for the defence of the country." I didn't see it -- where on that page that was being shown, and the answer that came thereafter. I tried to look, I couldn't see it. I see the page has now changed. I don't know ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- it is [In English] monitoring.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We moved that --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It was there on the page that I was looking at at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Sorry. [Interpretation] We apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's not your fault. It's ... it's the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I will just check something in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next thing I'm interested in is the following item: "Draws up, updates and inspects the plans of engagement of VJ?" Let me ask you General, what exactly is a plan of engagement of the army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The plan of engagement of the VJ is a complex document which must be made early on and defines how the army is to be used in war. It is the 1st Administration that is tasked with drafting these plans and it does so in organisation with -- in -- sorry, in coordination with all organisational units of the General Staff. It is the only unit authorised to keep those plans and controls them in the subordinate units. It also monitors the updating of those plans, in accordance with organisational changes performed in individual commands or units.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Right below that, there's something that we will discuss later, and it refers to the border service. But let me ask you first: How do you explain the following tasks? It is charged with the drafting of the plan of strategic camouflage.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: We all know that all armies in the world, which certainly includes the Army of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, try to keep its plans of engagement secret, so as to prevent intelligence services to come by that information. That is why the plan of operative and strategic camouflage is made. It means, very briefly, that this plan is meant to deceive the possible adversary with regard to our real intents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like this document to be marked for identification because we don't yet have a full English translation. But once we get it, we'll tender it into evidence. I don't intend to ask the witness anything else about this document. As I said, this is 001114D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence and marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D200, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see document 01129D on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is an extract about the internal organisation of the 1st Administration, which is your administration, sir. Can you see the document on the screen in front of you, Mr. Simic? If not, I can provide a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this about?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What this is about, I have described to you how a certain organisational structure is developed. We can see from this document that the chief of sector requested all administrations to submit their view on the future organisational structure and the functional tasks of their respective administrations. I drafted this with my co-workers and submitted it to the head of sector which will integrate all such proposals at the level of the entire sector and the -- the following procedure is as described before.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to see page 7 of the B/C/S version, and page 6 of the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm only interested in two organisational units on which I would like your comments, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please enlarge the B/C/S text, the second paragraph, for the General to see better.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm interested to hear from you about the tasks and authority of the state border sector.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This sector -- or, actually, section is an organisational unit of the 1st Administration. It has the basic task of regulating, monitoring the situation and proposing that certain measures be taken to the end of securing the state border. At the level of -- of an army, we had organs for the border service. All the reports from the border organs were forwarded along the chain of command. They were subordinate to the commander of the army, and the officer in charge of state border-related issues would forward it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us be more precise. Which chain of command exactly are we now referring to, with regard to this organisational unit of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: When it comes to professional expertise, border units are linked with the border section of the 1st Administration. In the chain of command, they are linked with the corps commanders or army commanders respectively, in their respective zones of responsibility.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more organisational unit about which we will speak more extensively during your testimony is one more thing I'm interested in. Tell us, please, what is the operative centre of the General Staff of the VJ? Can you explain to the Trial Chamber in simple terms.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The operative centre of the General Staff of the VJ is also an organisational unit of the 1st Administration, which exclusively deals with the collection of information from the territory, territorial waters and air-space of other federal organs in the country and, together with them, drafts reports about the information so collected for certain persons in the General Staff. It has a staff of 13 experienced officers with a rank of colonel, with abundant experience in the units or the staffs of armies and corps. They needed at least 20 years of experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We'll speak about this document -- these documents some more. But what was their -- what were their working hours?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The operative centre works round the clock, seven days a week. It has such equipment and materiel that enable it to be in -- to have communication with all subordinate army commands and also with the federal institutions in charge, such as the office of the minister of defence and the operative centre of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, the centre for information and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have an exhibit number for this document? There's no need for me to ask questions about the remainder of the document at the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D201. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now pass onto another document and another task of yours. Was one of the tasks of the 1st Administration drafting the plans of activities of the General Staff of the VJ for a certain period?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: I have mentioned, among others, that there was a department for operative and general planning. It was via this department that the 1st Administration drafted monthly and annual plans of activities of the General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see document 65 ter 00966D, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 966D.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can give you a hard copy, General, if you want, or maybe we can enlarge it on the screen. I think it will be better to give you a hard copy. Who is the author of this document? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it, but I'm waiting for you to fulfil your promise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just wanted to make use of the time while we're waiting. What is this document, Mr. Simic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This document is an accompanying document which I, as a chief of the 1st Administration of the General Staff, signed. There's a distribution list, and you can see to who it was distributed, to all organisational units of the General Staff, and those immediately subordinated in the chain of command; directly subordinated to the chief of General Staff, that is. You can see that 22 copies were made and to who it was distributed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us be precise. Under 22 of the -- in the distribution list, who is that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: It is the inspection of the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But above that, 22?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The federal Ministry of Defence. No, it is not subordinated. But I mentioned that there was cooperation and, therefore, it was required for certain organisational units of the ministries to be informed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to the following page in both language versions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You asked the question who is number 22 on the distribution list. I don't see a number 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please tell us, although it says here, to who was this plan forwarded and who approves it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see page 3 in the English, please. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us, whose responsibility was it to approve this plan? On page 2, you can see it in the left corner.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This work-plan is approved by the Chief of the General Staff. It was made by the 1st Administration in cooperation with other organisational units, and I forwarded it to all relevant units who were meant to implement it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see on page 3 of the B/C/S and on page 4 of the English - if we could have that on our screens - that there are general goals and specific goals, but I don't want to dwell on that because it can be read easily. But, now, let's go to B/C/S page 4 and page 5 of the English. Could you please comment -- let's just wait for it to appear on the screen. So here's what I'm interested in. Could you please comment on these priority tasks. How do you explain them in relation to what is written here on this page, under 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Here you can see that we define in global terms what a general goal was, what special goals were, and then those served to define tasks. And within the scope of the tasks not all the tasks carry the same specific weight, and that's why we expressed, under C, what our priority tasks were. I can say that two-thirds of the forces and resources of the Army of Yugoslavia were to be used to deal with the priority tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please comment upon the first priority task, only the first one.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The first priority task is similar to what I said about the operations centre. It says here: Monitor and assess the military and political situation in the country and in the surrounding area. And then proposes the taking of relevant measures with a view to raising combat readiness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why does it say here that the situation has to be monitored and assessed primarily in the crisis areas of the country and the areas of the seceded republics? Why was that important?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: You are leading me to talk about details, and I said in the country, in the immediate surroundings, which also implies what you've just stated. In the seceded republics there was a civil war going on, and such a situation could have an adverse impact on the security of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. That is why the tasks -- the task takes priority. And there is another task which mentions crisis areas within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please just say a few sentences as to what was happening in the 1994 and 1995, and what was considered crisis areas?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: A reference was being made in the media about a possible armed rebellion in Kosovo and Metohija, and we used that term "crisis areas" when referring to that territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 7 in B/C/S, as well as in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We see some tables here and let's provide the Trial Chamber with some information which will help them analyse the document at a later stage. Could you please tell us a few words about what we see on the pages before us.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This is a tabular part of the annual plan. In the left-hand side column, we can what the basis for the task was. The first task, it says the order of the Chief of General Staff and a reference is made to its number. The second column is the name of the task or, rather, what needs to be done. Column 4 provides the task code which ties it to the rest of the plans. Number 5 is who is responsible for the task. This is very important for us. The person or body responsible is the administration or the organisational unit which is fully responsible for the performance of the task, irrespective of the fact that there are others -- other organisational units cooperating as associated organisation. It may be just one organisational unit or more than one. Then in column 7, you can see how the task will be verified and it is usually done by the collegium of the chiefs of General Staff or the Deputy Chief of General Staff. And, finally, all tasks obviously have their deadlines within which they have to be carried out. Since this is an annual plan, deadlines are expressed in months. And in monthly plans, the task is broken down and the plan provides the exact number of things that will be done in one month.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please consult your hard copy and tell us who signed the document? Look at the last page of your B/C/S document.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: It was the Deputy Chief of General Staff. That was, at the moment, when the function of a deputy was introduced. Before that, such a document would have been signed by the assistant Chief of General Staff for operations and staff affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document into evidence and I will no longer need it after that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. This document shall be assigned Exhibit D202. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that the time is good for our next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Thank you so much. We will take a break until half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will move on to a different topic, and we will leave the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia aside.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce 65 ter 00611D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of the term "the staff of the supreme commander of the Army of Yugoslavia," and can you explain the term to us? What is it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Not only did I hear of it, but I also know that, according to our theory and our doctrine, the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, during the times of war and under an immediate threat of war, it is transformed from the peacetime establishment into the staff of the supreme commander and deployed in several command posts at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When an immediate threat of war -- when was the immediate threat of war and war declared in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Don't have to give us the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the NATO aggression?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did anything to that effect happen before?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Before that, the state of war was never declared. Not during the period while General Perisic was in position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down. Slow down. Again, you're speaking both at the same time and the interpreter is having serious problems, okay? You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is it exactly what I asked you. When you said the aggression, when did that happen, in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you're saying while General Perisic was the Chief of General Staff and before that, do you know whether the state of war or an immediate threat of war was ever declared?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: While General Perisic was the Chief of General Staff, neither of the two was ever declared.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when Zivota Panic was the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Not even then.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's look at a document which is on the screen before you. Would you like to receive it in a hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, please. It will be easier. The screen is too far.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will have a hard copy for each of the documents that we will call up. I already showed you this document during your preparations for testimony. It was signed by the then-Chief of General Staff, Zivota Panic, in 1993, and in the preamble you can see that it says: "Based on the tasks for the transformation of the Yugoslav Army, the changes effected in the command system and demonstrated need, the Chief of the General Staff of the Yugoslav Army hereby issues," and so on and so forth. An order on the establishment and makeup of the staff of the supreme commander of the Yugoslav Army. Could you provide any comment to this document. Do you know whether that staff of the Supreme Command existed? Why did it exist if there was no immediate threat of war, if there was no state of war declared at the time?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: I feel a bit embarrassed to comment upon the preceding period. However, the preamble itself does not have its legal foundation for such a wording of this document. As I already told you, the staff of the supreme commander, during a war or under an immediate threat of war, exists and the composition that can you see in this document is a collegium. Actually, it is a body composed of chiefs of General Staff which is just called with a different name. In order for a command or staff to function as a staff of the Supreme Command, it has to be split into several unities. Let me not go that way. And in this particular case, this wasn't the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In essence?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: In essence, nothing was changed with the change of name. Nothing is changed from the aspect of the methods of work of the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean -- you mean the collegium?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D203. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now could the witness please be shown P727. We have prepared a hard copy for the witness, to be provided to the witness while the document is being called up.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You don't have to tell us the date, but tell us when Mr. Perisic became the Chief of the General Staff of the Army of Yugoslavia, approximately?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: General Perisic became the Chief of General Staff sometime in August 1993, towards the end of August of that year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when we were talking about your CV earlier today, after that, you became the chief of the 1st Administration in the autumn of that year?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes. That same year, in November, pursuant to his order I was appointed the chief of the 1st Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Look at this document. I would like to you comment upon it just briefly. This document was signed by General Perisic. And on page 1 -- could you please comment upon the contents of the first page?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This document, issued by the Chief of General Staff, was aimed at regulating the implementation of certain tasks. And to explain this a bit better, this is actually a method of work to be adopted by the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You mean the collegium?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, the collegium of the Chief of General Staff and the organisational units. This document defines when, on what days things will be done. For example, on Monday will be one thing; on Fridays something else; on Wednesday a certain activity in the administration and so on and so forth. And it also schedules the meetings of the collegium.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know, at least approximately, I'm not looking for the exact date, when the collegiums of the chief of General Staffs started being operational and replaced the staff of the supreme commander?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, General Perisic continued functioning, pursuant to that order issued by General Panic, all the way up to perhaps February or March 1994. And then the collegium was established. He renamed that body into a collegium, and that's how things were done thereafter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here we can see daily meetings, weekly meetings and monthly meetings. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Daily meetings, as we can see, let us not quote, comprised a certain number of persons whom you can see here. There are also weekly meetings and topics, as well as monthly meetings. In a period thereafter, when the collegium started being operational, did it maintain the similar form of daily, weekly and monthly meetings?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: By and large. But he also defined some other contents which were not appropriate for the staff of the Supreme Command. For example, on Wednesday, there was briefing across the board of all administrations and so on and so forth. And that's why I used the term "similarities" between the former document and this document. This document, however, is more appropriate for the daily operational command. That's the term that you used. And we, when we defined things, we called it a method of work of the Chief of General Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of the same document, could you please look at it just briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the English, just bear with me, please. I believe it's the last English page. I believe it's the same page, page 3. I don't know whether the Trial Chamber -- could the previous page be displayed for the Trial Chamber. Could you perhaps scroll up the English version a little. I don't know whether this is the end of that page or not. Can we see the top of the page, please? That's what I would like to see. Uh-huh. Yes, yes. Your Honours, I'm going ask the witness about the part beginning with the word: "The plan." Perhaps the Trial Chamber could first look at the English version of this page and maybe we can then turn to the following page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What is this?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the following page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, what is the page that you have before you, this page in this document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This is the plan work of one of the meetings of that staff of the supreme commander or, rather, the collegium, as we called it subsequently. And this plan defines the issues to be discussed by the collegium. People who will be presenting certain topics and the duration of the discussion. This was drafted by the office of the Chief of General Staff and it was approved by General Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And here reference is made to a certain number of topics following a certain sequence. Do you remember it that way, when collegiums of the Chief of General Staff -- this is how things were done. There was sequence of topics.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: That was more or less the sequence that was followed. At the beginning, the focus was on the situation and activities of a foreign countries and -- important for the Yugoslav Army and the security of Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. That was the sector of the chief of intelligence administration. Then activity of foreign intelligence services towards Yugoslav Army and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. This was presented by the chief of security, because that was his purview. And then, number 3, was combat readiness in the Army of Yugoslavia. The presenter was the appropriate officer, the usual suspect, I apologise for the pun.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will no longer need this document. We will move on to a different topic. This is already in evidence. And now I would like us to talk about the border duties. In one of the previous documents, we saw that the functioning of the border patrols was something that your administration was concerned with. First of all, let me ask you this: What were the changes that were affected with regard to the state border after the breakup of the SFRY and the establishment of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The initial changes had to do with the lack of definition of the state border facing particular former republics of the Federative Republic of Yugoslavia, to be more specific, the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The state border, as such, pursuant to international law, we all know what it is. I don't need to go there. And my department for state border was tasked with the security of the state border. I apologise for saying "my department." It was a department in the 1st Administration that I was the head of.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What were the names of the borders facing the Republic of Croatia and the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, as well as the Republic of Macedonia before the breakup of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down. Please slow down. The interpreters have serious problems. Yeah, if you take a breath every time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is a generally known fact that the Federative Republic of Yugoslavia had its republics and that those republics were separated by administrative borders. There came a time when Yugoslavia broke up as a federal state, and those borders became state borders. From the aspect of international law and from the aspect of our forces, materiel and equipment, this fact created a lot of problems when it came to providing security for such newly established state borders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why did that pose problems? What kind of problems?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The main problems arose from the fact that there was a lack of definition of that border. The state border-line was often determined, pursuant to the cadastre borders of the municipalities which was not a good enough proof that that was indeed the state border and that it mandated to be protected by the state. That was one problem. The second problem was the fact that from the year 1945, we did not have enough infrastructure on the borders facing other states. There were no agreements to that effect with the neighbouring states. There were no sentry posts. There was no technical equipment. The state borders did not function as such on the borders between the former republics. The population in those areas was not used to the fact that they are now living close to the state borders and they treated the orders of state borders in ways that could not have always been construed as correct and fair.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who was it who provided security for what parts of the state border?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The state border facing the Republic of Croatia, the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, was within the purview and I'm talking from the aspect of the highest levels, it was within the purview of the command of the 1st Army and the command of the 2nd Army. The command of the 1st Army was in Belgrade and the command of the 2nd Army was in Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Who had authority over border crossings and who was charged with securing them?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I should have said at the outset that there were rules in force about the border service, and that these rules clearly defined what is to be considered a border and what exactly a border crossing is, which organs had what kind of rights on the border-line or at the border crossing. To your specific question, I can provide the following answer. The Army of Yugoslavia was responsible for securing the state border outside border crossings and outside inhabited areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And when it comes to border crossings and inhabited or populated areas, under whose authority were they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: It was the MUP of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia that had authority over the border crossings, as well as the organs of the customs service. In populated areas -- or, rather, populated areas were under the authority of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you said MUP, that is what exactly?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: It's the Ministry of the Interior. I apologise. I will try to avoid abbreviations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, that's all right, but we must be precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please show document 01050D to the witness, from the 65 ter list of Defence documents. That is 65 ter 01050D.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I have no hard copy of this document so I will ask General Simic to look closely at the screen. You have seen it already, sir, so you should be familiar with it. But it will be enlarged any moment now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please enlarge somewhat the B/C/S version?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It seems we won't be able to do so.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: No, it's okay. I'm familiar with this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If we could first -- or maybe let me read it out. Let us take a look at this second page to see who signed the document and then I will read a few sentences and ask you for a comment. And that seems to be the simplest way of proceeding. You have been able to see by the letterhead that it was sent from the office of the Chief of General Staff, and now please tell us who signed it.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Colonel Ivan Todorovic, the chief of the office.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will now go back to the first page from which I will read to the witness. I will only read out extracts. This document is called, The engagement of the Army of Yugoslavia in securing the border to ensure the peace and safety of citizens in the Pljevlja municipality. It is sent to the office of the defence minister. We can see why this document was drafted. And now, in paragraph 2, we read: "It is strictly regulated in Article 48, paragraph 1, of the Law of Crossing the State Border and Movement in the Border Area," and then we see references to the Official Gazette, "that border army units shall secure the state border and control the movement and stay of persons in the border area outside populated places and border crossings, to prevent unauthorised crossing of the state border and violations of the border-line." Does this correspond to what you have said a minute ago?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Under Article 2 of the same law: "The border zone shall include the 100-metre-wide area of the FRY territory, land, rivers and lakes along the border-line." Before I continue with the document, do tell us what the border-line is?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The border-line is the that separates the territories of two neighbouring countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now the securing of the border-line in depth, as it is phrased here. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: I would have to say what you have also read out, the border belt, or the border area. That is, from the border-line, 100 metres deep into our territory, that area is called the border belt. In that border belt, the army has the right to deprive any person of their liberty, if that person has no permit for staying in the border belt. After the official procedure, such a person is handed over to the MUP organs. Securing the border-line in depth means the following. Since we don't have a line of soldiers along the border-line, so you can't see soldiers standing there at a certain distance from each other to secure the border-line, but, instead, we do so through organs. If the assessment is that along certain directions some groups may try to cross the border from a neighbouring country or that the border may be violated in another way, we deploy additional organs in the border belt and, thus, set up a -- an in-depth security structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will read out this last sentence of this letter: "The" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please start anew, a bit slower.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Counsel, the interpreter requests that you start again but go slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we have it on the screen. I apologise to the interpreters. I will read out that part again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "The area outside the border belt is within the jurisdiction of the organs of the internal affairs which are responsible for preventing any unlawful action and securing of personal and material property and peace of all citizens of the FRY, including those of Pljevlja municipality." This corresponds to what you have said a short while ago, namely, that everything outside the border belt is under the authority of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Outside the border belt, the VJ has no authority. Even if they were to observe certain persons committing violations, they have no legal authority to intervene. But they can inform the nearest police station using communications equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I suppose it's their duty too.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's their duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now -- Your Honours, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution objects to the admission of this document for two reasons. First of all, my colleague Mr. Simic [sic] has read substantial portions of the document into the record already, and so I believe, according to the practice of this Chamber, there is no need for this document to be admitted. Second of all, I note from the top of the document it is titled a draft reply, so once again, Your Honour, I don't see what the probative value of this document will be, what weight could be given to it. It was someone's draft, we don't whether it was adopted, we don't know what happened to it, we don't know whether it was agreed upon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, I guess when your colleague on the opposite side, he said his colleague Mr. Simic, he meant his colleague Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was reading the document, although I know that is not in accordance with your guide-lines, Your Honours, but for purely practical reasons because we were unable to show it to the witness on the screen, and also to enable to you follow. But this document says things that have a certain value. If we read the first paragraph, why this document was written, I didn't ask the witness about the reasons. I just wanted his testimony about the material parts of this document and he confirm the authenticity and the significance of this document. I take it to be very relevant and clearly shows the -- the -- under whose purview the border belt was, so I don't see why we shouldn't admit it for the purpose of this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You're not answering to the issues raised by your colleague. Your colleague raises two objections why we shouldn't admit it. One, you have read into the record, so there's no need in terms of the guide-lines. Two, it's a draft and not a final document. That's what he says. Now when you pull your face as if are you hearing it for the first time, you surprise me. So you have got to address those two objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for the first objection, I replied that I read out the document to the witness because that was the way to familiarize him with it and also to enable the Trial Chamber to follow it on the transcript. And as for the second objection, whether this is a draft document or not, this can possibly pertain to the probative value of the document. But drafts of some decisions can also be evidence, for which there is -- for which there are previous examples. So whether or not this is a draft is irrelevant for the probative value of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are explaining why you read it. You are not answering why it should be admitted, if it has been read. The guide-lines says when the document has been read, there's no need to admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Then I didn't correctly understand Mr. Saxon's objection, or yours. I didn't read out the entire document, only two paragraphs, so that's why I would like to tender the document, because I believe that other paragraphs are also relevant and I didn't read them out, because those parts of the document are self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If we mark it for identification, can you get the approved document, not the draft?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honours. This -- whether subsequently a -- an official letter of the Ministry of the Defence was produced based on this draft is a different matter. But the very fact that this draft was signed by somebody has a certain weight. But whether or not this was indeed sent to the municipal -- to the municipality in Pljevlja really is of no interest to anybody here. I don't believe it is relevant for the procedure, whether this -- the minister of defence actually sent a letter to the president of Pljevlja municipality. But what we are interested in is the contents of the document, as it speaks about the border belt and related issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: True, Mr. Lukic. And there is nothing in the objection that refers to this document being sent to the municipality of -- whatever this town is called. The objection is that this is a draft. It is not known whether this is an official document of the department that claims to have produced it because it is still in -- in a draft form. Whether or not it was sent is immaterial. And that was the objection that you've got to address and tell us why, notwithstanding the fact that it is in draft form, it has got to be exhibited. That it is signed is neither here nor there, if it is a draft.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I put a question to the witness in order to clarify?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you can, yeah, go ahead [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the first page of the document? In B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, I'm going to read to you what it says. It says: "The engagement of the VJ in providing security for the border belt in order to secure peace and order for the municipality of Pljevlja." Submitted to the office of the minister of defence. Could you please comment? Is this just a draft of the proposal or is it a draft that was signed by the chief of the office of the Ministry of Defence for their further action, to be taken by them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you are going to ask -- well, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I object to the leading nature of that question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think I was leading.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this an official document stamped and duly recorded?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: With the Trial Chamber's permission, I would provide a somewhat lengthier answer. The --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you please just answer the specific question before that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Will you allow me, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No. Your lawyer says please answer the specific question before you do that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was sent on the part of the General Staff to the Ministry of Defence. The implementation or the solution to those problems was not within the authority of the Chief of General Staff and that's why it was referred for further proceedings to the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Is this an official document?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it practice, sir, in this department to send official documents in draft form? It says -- your lawyer read something to you but didn't read this part, which is written in capital letters, which says: "Draft reply." It's not a reply; it's a draft. Is that how you send out documents, as drafts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Really?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission I can explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But we've been seeing documents here that you've been testifying to, they're not written "draft." This is the first one that is written "draft."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Your Honours, I can explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I interfere, please? I can see that we are facing a problem and the problem arises from the English interpretation or translation, rather. I would like to go over --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The problem arises from the fact that, instead of responding to an objection, you asked to ask a question. Now we're getting involved in talking to a witness instead of you responding to an objection. That's the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I read what is stated in the heading to the witness and then I look at the English version, you are basing your questions and Mr. Saxon is basing his objections to the -- on the English version, and I believe that the whole problem arises from that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... we can't read the B/C/S. [Overlapping speakers] ... that's why you've got it here for us to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I appreciate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read for the transcript and I believe that the interpreters have interpreted what I have read. I will read it once again. I would kindly ask the interpreters and I'm sure that they appreciate what the problem is. The title reads: "The engagement of the Army of Yugoslavia in providing security for the border in order to provide peace and security of the citizens of Pljevlja municipality. Draft proposal to be sent to."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Rather, draft reply, the interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well? Isn't that what the English says?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I think that we have a bit of a confusion here. I'm not blaming the interpreters but --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you please explain, Mr. Simic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, since the Ministry of Defence was not authorised to provide security for the state border, the municipal assembly of Pljevlja faced certain problems and turned to the minister of defence. Before that, the minister of defence turned to the Chief of General Staff for his opinion about the problem. And if you look at the document, you can see that we defined what the responsibility of the army was and how far did that responsibility reach. And as for the other problems put forth by the Municipal Assembly of Pljevlja, we told them that the body responsible was the Ministry of the Interior and its organs, in that municipality. And that is why there is an annex to that letter, entitled: A proposal for a possible reply which contained our responsibility. There was no organ or body within the ministry that would have been in charge of the state borders. And here, the problems that the municipality of Pljevlja was facing, as represented by the Municipal Assembly, and they believed that the army could help them. That's why we submitted our proposal. It was not requested from us to provide a final response.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: One more subquestion. This document of yours, is this a draft or is this a final document which somebody else had to copy and formulate?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: For us, as the General Staff, this was a final version of that document. And for the person who had to draft their document for the Municipal Assembly, that was just a proposal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence, marked for identification, until you give us a correct translation of the document. If is a draft proposal and not a draft reply, you will have to give us a correct interpretation of the document. May it please be given an exhibit number and marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D204, marked for identification. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The next document that I would like to look at with the witness is 0 -- 65 ter 00891D, from the same batch and dealing with the same topic. But before I look at this document, I would like to talk about another period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know that at one point the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia introduced sanctions in respect of Republika Srpska? Do you know when that was and what were the sanctions about? If you know.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia introduced sanction in respect of Republika Srpska and that was sometime in August 1994. And the sanctions applied to the interruption of all flows of goods with the exception of humanitarian aid.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the Army of Yugoslavia honoured the decision of the government of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia concerning the sanctions?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, fully.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's look at a document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could the witness please be provided with a hard copy of the document and the others can follow the English version on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Tell me, General, who is Gojko Knezevic? Do you know? Does the name ring a bell?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Of course. He was my most immediate associate. Gojko Knezevic was a colonel, and he was the chief of the 3rd department or the department in charge of operative and general planning in the 1st Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We already discussed the document, to two of us, during your preparations. Could you please tell us a few words about the contents of the document. The document was issue in the November 1994 and was prompted by something that happened in that month. What was that and what was the connection between your administration and the activities described herein?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This is a document -- or, rather, an order ordering the control and securing the state border facing Republika Srpska in the area of responsibility of the 1st and 2nd Armies. The intention behind the document was to implement the sanctions, and since this was a newly established state border, we wanted to take stock of all problems, and the priority was given to the work of state border security organs and how they implemented the measures introduced by the federal government with regard to the sanctions. And this here is a report from one of the controls, pointing to some of the problems that I myself had pointed out when I was speaking in general terms as to what problems we were facing with regard to the newly established state borders. And you can also see from this document how the army and troops carried out their tasks. You can see that there were some shortcomings and omissions that would be removed in the future period.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D205. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, could the Court please produce -- just a moment, please. Bear with me. 65 ter 00881D. We have a hard copy for the witness, for Mr. Simic. Could he please be provided with the hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: First tell us, please, who the signatory of the document was.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The document was signed by the Deputy Chief of General Staff, General Blagoje Kovacevic. And the document deals with the development of the system of security of the state border and attempts to remove our subjective problems. In a nutshell, it was about dealing with problems with the structures of society on the ground, and in this letter he defined the tasks, he -- and he also defined the deadlines.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What I would like to draw your attention to in this document is the title and the preamble. What territory and what state border does this document refer to and highlights?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This document refers to the border facing Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the meaning of the order can be found in the preamble. For the purpose of eliminating weaknesses and securing the border more efficiently, especially with Republika Srpska, the order is issued and measures requested. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document also be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned colleague Mr. Lukic has not established any relationship between the witness and this document. Mr. Lukic just read the first -- what is stated on the first line. He has had the witness confirm what is in the document. But there has been no relationship established between this witness and this document. According to the guide-lines, then it should not be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just respond. I believe that I did establish sufficient link between the witness and the document, because the witness has already spoken about the significance of state borders. I don't intend to testify. I don't want to mention other things that are visible in the document which are so closely linked to the witness. I don't see the need to continue exploring the document further, but if you wish me to do so, I can do that. However, from what -- from all that we heard about the authorities of the witness, about his administration, I believe that this document is so self-evident that there is it absolutely no need to put any additional questions, in order to establish a -- a -- a link between the witness and the document. And my answer, in a nutshell, is simple. I believe that I did establish a good enough link between the document and the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you show us on the transcript where you established the link, Mr. Lukic, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked him who the signatory of the document was, and he replied --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Show us on the transcript where you asked that question. Page -- page -- page 82, line 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 82. And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: He is telling us about the signatory, yes, but does that tell us about the link between himself and the document, if I must go to the objection by your learned friend?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we saw from his earlier evidence that there is a sufficient link between the witness and the document, because the witness recognised the signature of his superior, and according to the standards of -- of evidence, I believe I have established a sufficient link. I don't think that we need to establish whether the witness is familiar with the document but merely set up a relationship between the witness and the document, which I believe we have explicitly done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You say the witness told us it was signed by his superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I previously asked him in the previous session about whether or not Mr. Kovacevic was his superior. In the previous session, when I asked about the chief of that sector, and the witness replied that it was Mr. Kovacevic. I had hoped that everybody in the courtroom would have remembered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I may add, what the witness said about problems also can be seen in the documents, so that the witness is familiar with the subject matter of the document and that is the problems related to border control.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: But I think what Mr. Lukic just said is really testimony, Your Honour, because it didn't come out of the mouth of this witness with respect to this document. And quite frankly, if confirming that a particular person has signed a document which everyone can see is the test for a relationship, then I submit that's a pretty low test indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Lukic is also saying that Mr. Kovacevic was the witness's superior, and he recognises the signature of his superior, it comes from the same department, and he is familiar also with the contents. This witness is -- is that what you said he was testifying about?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I beg out on that one, then. Mr. Lukic, apparently are you testifying about the knowledge that this witness has about the contents of the document. Apparently the witness has not said so himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not, Your Honours. We can go back to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You can go back to page 82, line 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 82, yes. And what follows is the witness's reply where he described everything, and I merely repeated the witness's words. Between lines 13 and 18, the witness gave evidence about these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have anything to say on that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Nothing further, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you still stand on your objection, notwithstanding that?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will withdraw that objection, Your Honour. I've been corrected by Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D206. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Simic, take a look at yet another document that deals with the same topic as the 65 ter document 00882D. I will also provide a hard copy for you. General, can you tell us whose document this is? Do you recognise the signatory?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: This is a document of the General Staff of the VJ, signed by the Chief of the General Staff, General Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We can see a stamp that it was recorded. Where was -- what was the route of this document before it reached the Chief of General Staff?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Since securing the state border is within the purview of the 1st Administration, this document was drafted in the 1st Administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will merely read out item 1 of this letter, and I'll ask you to comment on it. It was sent to the commands of the 1st and 2nd Army, and to the navy command. Item 1 says: "Fully implement all orders of the Chief of Staff of the VJ on securing the state border towards the Republic of Croatia and the Republika Srpska, and prevent any individuals from crossing the state border outside border crossings. This applies, in particular, to the border in the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Army and of the navy." Could you please comment on this paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The Chief of General Staff, here again, stresses the importance of securing the state border in the complex circumstances that prevailed then, especially in areas where the configuration of terrain was demanding. There was a part of our border with Croatia in -- around Herceg-Novi and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That -- that's the navy?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And what is the zone of responsibility of the 2nd Army?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: The border with Republika Srpska up to north of Pljevlja. At Pljevlja there was the 1st Border Battalion, or, rather, there was the 7th Border Battalion, but it was the first unit -- the unit closest to the zone of responsibility of the 1st Army, if we look southward.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "If there are border crossings in the zone of responsibility that are not manned by MUP employees, warn the MUP of their obligation and insist that they fulfill it immediately." Is that in line with what you said earlier, that the MUP was -- had responsibility for border crossings?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. But in these complex circumstances, when there were no border posts or defined crossings and when these crossings were not adequately manned, there were some problems. The Chief of General Staff, bearing in mind the decisions taken by the highest state authorities about imposing sanctions, wanted to warn his subordinates once more of the seriousness of their tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: General, we will speak about the operative centre later and the Trial Chamber will be acquainted with border-related reports. But let me ask you a general question now. Have you heard of members of the VJ misusing the regime prevalent in the -- along the border? It had to do with the responsibility of the border services.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: I have no knowledge of any organs of the border service of the -- of VJ as not carrying out their duties in full compliance with orders and instructions received from the highest authorities. I cannot rule out, however, that there may have been individual violations of the border-line from either side, because, as I have explained, they were controlled by organs that were a kilometre, or two, or five away from each other. So they were in a position to watch, have visual control, patrol the border, et cetera, but it may have happened that somebody crossed the border, nonetheless. However, generally speaking, we fully implemented the decisions of the highest authorities systemically.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you say "systemically," what was the position of General Perisic with regard to the border service?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: General Perisic, at that time, gave special attention to the securing of the border with the former republics of Yugoslavia. There were two aspects to that: That we were not to act in contravention of the orders of the supreme commander; and, secondly, we should -- we should not allow for the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to be threatened by any activities that may be taking place on the other side of the border.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What kind of activities were they?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG SIMIC
utterances.text: If, in the immediate vicinity, combat activities were going on, armed groups, or paramilitary formations, or army or military units could cross the border and commit some acts. That is why the Chief of General Staff wanted to prevent any major excesses that could detrimentally affect our safety and security. And, in that context, the border service were the first ones to monitor not only our territory but also what was going on across the border, and they would report on everything they observed which was relevant for the security of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit D207. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I now wish to board a completely different topic so this may be a convenient time for us to adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will take an adjournment. And, sir, before we adjourn, I must warn you that as you have now taken the witness-stand, you may not discuss the case with anybody, in particular, not with your lawyers, okay, until you have finished testifying. You must come back tomorrow, in the afternoon, at quarter past 2.00, in the same courtroom, Courtroom II. Court adjourned until tomorrow, quarter past 2.00, Courtroom II.
